parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national document/entry layer with division-level care and violence evidence. Foreign posts must refuse cases casting doubt on an applicant's sex and may pursue lifetime fraud ineligibility; X-markers are barred and travellers report confiscation and strandings, prompting eight foreign advisories. Federal custody is documented harm: conversion-therapy-style prison policy and abuse of trans immigrants. Facility bans cover 21 units nationally, but this division's status is undocumented. Locally: under-18 care banned, adult surgery cancelled in one city, and killings of trans women recorded only as an undercounted floor without a denominator. Protections (hate-crime statute, employment ruling, marriage equality, enjoined orders, pending suits) exist but are contested and uneven. No identity criminalisation, but state exposure dominates.

entry_documents.exposure: X-markers barred for new passports/visas (Feb 2025), M/F only; Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscation/stranding; eight foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; national civil-liberties suit pending; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, investigation and detention, where custody policies then apply; the division cannot override federal passport and visa control.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections bureau mandates conversion-therapy-style policy for trans inmates (hair cut, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution); trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse by guards.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for visitors. Several national orders are enjoined, but the custody policies are reported as operating.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor refused entry or detained after a document/sex-doubt finding enters the same federal custody system; division authority provides no shelter.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National map (Nov 2026): 21 units restrict gender-identical facility use, 6 extend bans to some private settings, 4 make it criminal in certain circumstances; one documented trespass arrest of a trans woman (2025) with 24 hours in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; map notes other sex-definition laws may still affect access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whether this division bans facility use is not stated; federal funding and rhetoric push units toward restriction, and the map warns of unmapped policies.

care_services.exposure: Division bans under-18 hormone therapy/surgery (in force 1 July 2023, licence revocation penalty); a coastal hospital cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries 13 Feb 2025, including a 24-year-old adult's pre-approved procedure, citing state and national law; national funding freezes and proposed insurance bar.
care_services.protection: Public-employee health plan settlement (Oct 2023) covers medically necessary gender-affirming care and can reach out-of-state care for minors — resident-facing only.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or continued care meets narrowed adult capacity and post-Jan-2025 provider caution; emergency-ward treatment by identity is not documented either way.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders call youth care 'mutilation', direct law enforcement to investigate schools promoting 'gender ideology', a 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender', and a 2025 poll shows 66% backing birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The rewards memo lists 'radical gender ideology' only as rhetoric, never as a reward criterion; counterterrorism text says powers won't target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that document or facility encounters escalate and lowers the expected sympathy of officials handling a reported incident.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division prohibits transition care for under-18s from licensed clinicians; national order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition and bars federally funded youth services; a travelling trans minor faces the same document, entry and facility layers.
minors_guardians.protection: Grandfather clause lets minors on HRT before 1 July 2023 continue; public-employee plan can pay for minors' care obtained outside the division.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor carries both travellers' document exposure at the border, plus the division's care ban if treatment is needed during the visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Major city recorded 4.8 per 100k killings of trans women, explicitly an undercount floor with no general-homicide denominator — per rubric, no usable rate; 2023 saw two fatal shootings a week apart and one attempted murder, with police calling violence 'epidemic-level'.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police openly investigated the 2023 cases; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 units extend bias-motivated-violence statutes to gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Federal hate-crime coverage may reach a visitor's assault, but state bias-statute coverage is partial and outcomes of the 2023 investigations are unrecorded.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation on passports, executive orders and health rules unresolved; division care-ban challenge outcome unknown; 2023 investigation outcomes unrecorded; whether the surgery cancellation persists is unsourced; enforcement varies by moment of travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties suits, a legal-aid FAQ on document rules, court injunctions against several orders, and a functioning federal judiciary document partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy exists at the national courts even where agencies and hospitals impose the exposure, but no documented remedy reverses a visa refusal or custody placement in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Above 0.25-A: that profile has routine police raids, hotel sweeps and street extortion with officials treating complaints as complainant misconduct. Here there are no documented street raids or police extortion of visitors; hostility is institutional (entry refusal, custody policy) rather than pervasive street coercion, though custody abuse is comparably severe.

Close to 0.35-A: both combine a state-imposed universal exposure (their birth-sex public-building rule; our visa/sex-doubt refusal regime and custody practices) with no working remedy and polite private life. We lack a documented division-level facility ban, but add documented federal custody abuse of trans detainees, which 0.35-A does not.

Below 0.65-D: Tarelis has functioning police, a conviction for threatening a trans visitor, routine acceptance of foreign passports and no universal restriction. Our dossier documents an entry regime engineered to doubt an applicant's sex, federal custody harm and official threat-framing — heavier, more structural exposures than scattered service refusals.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: federal document and visa rules create a continuous discovery and refusal exposure (sex-doubt refusals, possible lifetime fraud finding, reported strandings, eight foreign advisories), and any escalation lands in federal custody where trans inmates lose hormones and trans immigration detainees report beatings and sexual abuse — state as perpetrator, tier 1–2. The division adds its own layer: under-18 care banned, adult surgery cancelled in one city, and killings of trans women recorded only as an undercounted floor, so no usable violence rate. Facility bans are national but undocumented for this division, an open question rather than an exposure. Protections (hate-crime statute, employment ruling, marriage equality, injunctions, pending suits) are real but contested and do not reverse a refusal or placement in time. Net: high risk, just above the 0.35 tier.
